stem:
A patient reports two days of early-pregnancy bleeding that has now settled. She has never had a scan confirming an intrauterine pregnancy. She is pain-free and haemodynamically stable. Transvaginal ultrasound shows neither an intrauterine nor an adnexal pregnancy and no free fluid. Serum hCG was 650 IU/L at presentation and is 720 IU/L 48 hours later.

How should the clinician classify and manage this pregnancy at present?

options.label: A
options.text: Complete miscarriage, as bleeding has settled and the uterus is empty
options.explanation: Complete miscarriage can be diagnosed only when an intrauterine pregnancy was previously seen. Without that, an empty uterus after bleeding may still hide an ectopic pregnancy.

options.label: B
options.text: Tubal ectopic pregnancy, so methotrexate can be started today
options.explanation: An 11% rise over 48 hours is suboptimal and raises concern for ectopic pregnancy, but no adnexal mass has been seen and the pattern also fits a failing intrauterine pregnancy. Giving methotrexate for an unconfirmed diagnosis risks harming a pregnancy that is not ectopic.

options.label: C
options.text: Probable viable intrauterine pregnancy, so rescan in two weeks
options.explanation: A viable intrauterine pregnancy usually shows a substantial rise in hCG over 48 hours; a near-plateau makes viability unlikely and a two-week wait unsafe.

options.label: D
options.text: Failed pregnancy, so she can be discharged without hCG follow-up
options.explanation: A failing pregnancy may be the cause, but hCG has not fallen and ectopic pregnancy has not been excluded, so stopping follow-up is unsafe.

options.label: E
options.text: Pregnancy of unknown location, with review and repeat hCG and scan
options.explanation: With no pregnancy seen on ultrasound, this remains a pregnancy of unknown location. The plateauing hCG makes a failing or ectopic pregnancy likely, so she needs senior review within 24 hours, repeat hCG and ultrasound, and clear advice to return with pain or bleeding.

context: An empty uterus without a previously confirmed intrauterine pregnancy is a pregnancy of unknown location; a plateauing hCG raises concern but does not diagnose ectopic pregnancy, so follow until resolved.
